subject: Post-call: Performance & SLO qualification — multi-region routing / data residency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finova.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance & SLO qualification — multi-region routing / data residency

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps so we’re aligned on requirements and what Redwood will validate during a short PoC.

TL;DR: Finova needs predictable p95 latency targets (interactive UX), support for streaming responses, and multi-region routing with EU data residency for EU traffic. Key numbers below — please confirm or correct.

Summary of requirements we captured:
- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end (client -> response complete) <= 220ms for text generation on typical prompt sizes (~100 tokens). For heavier prompts (>=512 tokens) target p95 <= 500ms.
- Throughput & concurrency: sustained 600 rps across peak hour, with burstable spikes to 1.2k rps. Concurrent long-lived streaming sessions ~150 (each streaming ~3–8s).
- Streaming: chunked token streaming required (server-sent events or HTTP/2). Must support both incremental tokens and a "response-ready" final event for UI reconciliation.
- Regional routing: route US traffic within US; EU traffic must stay in EU region (data at rest and logs). APAC traffic acceptable to route to nearest region (SG or JP) but preferred local residency for APAC-sensitive flows.
- Data residency & compliance: EU traffic must have logs and any persisted data (cache, KV) stored in EU; SOC2 and encryption-at-rest with customer KMS preferred for production.

Actions for Redwood (next steps):
1) Nikhil: produce an initial SLO/throughput matrix showing instance sizing and expected p95 for our recommended model config + quantization (attached: finova-slo-matrix.xlsx).
2) Marissa: follow up with a written proposal and propose dates for a 2-week PoC (producer/consumer test harness + traffic replay).
3) Alex/Priya: confirm final traffic split by region (US/EU/APAC %) and any additional security constraints (e.g., contract-level EU data residency clause).

Proposed timeline: PoC kickoff week of Mar 22, 2026 — we’ll validate p95 and throughput at target load, plus routing/fallback behavior.

If anything above is off, shout and I’ll update. Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: finova-slo-matrix.xlsx

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@finova.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & SLO qualification — multi-region routing / data residency

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: the 220ms p95 target is accurate for our main interactive flows (login -> challenge -> suggestion generation). For long-form generation (>=512 tokens) we can accept up to p95 700ms in PoC but prefer under 500ms in production.
- Throughput: 600 rps sustained is baseline. Our peak planning for Q3 assumes ~1.5k rps, so it would be helpful if the PoC includes a short spike test to 1.5k rps to understand autoscale behavior.
- Concurrency/streaming: the 150 concurrent streaming sessions estimate is correct. Each session will typically stream ~4–6 chunks over 2–6 seconds. We use SSE in our web client.
- Regional split (approx): US 62%, EU 30%, APAC 8%. EU traffic must remain in EU — includes request/response bodies, logs, and any persisted KV cache.
- Security: SOC2 is required; we will also request a data processing addendum (DPA) with EU data clauses. For production we will require envelope encryption with our KMS key (we can share the key metadata during contract negotiations).

We’re happy to proceed with the PoC week of Mar 22. One ask: can you include an option for model quantization choices (8-bit vs 4-bit) in Nikhil’s sizing matrix so we can evaluate quality vs cost?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | Finova
alex.turner@finova.com

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & SLO qualification — multi-region routing / data residency

Hi Alex — looping in a few technical details and what we’ll validate in the PoC.

High-level PoC plan (2-week):
- Week 1: baseline perf with production-ish prompt set (we’ll use traffic replay you provide), validate p50/p95/p99 for recommended model config.
- Week 2: scale & spike tests (sustained load to 600 rps, 3x short spike to 1.5k rps), validate streaming concurrency and autoscale/fallback behavior.

What Redwood will measure and deliver:
- End-to-end p95 with per-region breakdown (US/EU/APAC) including downstream network delta we observe.
- Throughput curve: rps -> p95/p99 delta for given instance types and configs (we’ll provide expected rps per GPU).
- Concurrency limits per node and recommended shard count for 150 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Streaming delivery: confirm compatibility with SSE and provide guidance for backpressure handling (buffer size, keepalive).
- Data residency: for PoC we’ll stand up EU-only instances (data at rest & logs in eu-central) and configure KV cache to use EU-backed persistence. For production we’ll enable customer KMS integration for envelope encryption.

Questions for Finova (action items):
1) Please share a small traffic sample (1–2 hours) and the prompt set you care about. We’ll use that to size and run replay.
2) Which models do you want in scope for the PoC? We recommend testing one medium-latency model + one quantized cost-optimized variant to compare latency/quality.

I’ll attach an initial sizing sheet and expected instance counts based on your throughput targets; Marissa will follow up with scheduling.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-multi-region-routing-overview.pdf

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@finova.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & SLO qualification — multi-region routing / data residency

All looks good — thanks for the clear plan. We’ll: 
- Upload a 2-hour traffic sample + prompt set to the secure S3 bucket you mentioned by EOD Thursday (I’ll send the link to Nikhil directly).
- Confirm model candidates by Friday (leaning toward medium-latency x-large and a 4-bit quantized cost option).
- Legal will draft the DPA and we’ll flag the KMS requirement in the contract comments.

PoC kickoff week of Mar 22 works for us. Please send a calendar invite with a brief pre-kickoff sync (30m) and an agenda — Marissa?

Thanks — Alex
